item.title: Promoting Pacific Prosperity: U.S. Engagement at the Pacific Islands Forum
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Promoting Pacific Prosperity: U.S. Engagement at the Pacific Islands Forum

Media Note

September 1, 2026

The United States is a Pacific nation and has long stood with our Pacific friends and neighbors to advance a free and open Indo-Pacific region.  Our commitment to the security and prosperity of the Pacific Islands is steadfast, enduring, and a key pillar of our America First Foreign Policy.

On September 1, at the Pacific Islands Forum Partners Dialogue in Palau, Deputy Secretary Christopher Landau announced over $150 million in U.S. support for Pacific Islands.  He delivered this message directly to our partners, engaging with Pacific Islands leaders and ministers to reinforce the depth and durability of U.S. partnerships in the region and announcing new U.S.-funded projects and investments in the Pacific Islands that aim to deliver economic prosperity and security for Americans and Pacific Islanders. 

The United States’ continued participation in the Pacific Islands Forum reflects the importance we place on the Pacific Islands as a vital part of the Indo-Pacific region.  When the Pacific Islands are stable, secure and prosperous, the United States is too.  Under President Trump and Secretary Rubio’s leadership, we are prioritizing commercial diplomacy and reorienting our foreign assistance programs in the Pacific around championing U.S. enterprise and investments in enabling infrastructure that supports private sector-led economic growth.  

Ensuring Energy Security

  • Regional Energy Security Initiative: Working with Congress, the Department intends to provide $60 million to help Pacific Islands countries address the ongoing global energy crisis, including expanding fuel storage capacity and supporting grid stability.
  • Fuel Supply Infrastructure for Tonga: The U.S. Trade and Development Agency (USTDA), with funding from the U.S. Department of State, will strengthen fuel supply reliability and energy security through a feasibility study to upgrade Tonga’s port facilities, fuel storage capacity, pipeline infrastructure and market-oriented regulatory practices.

Building Critical Infrastructure

  • Palau Hospital Relocation: The United States, Australia, Japan, New Zealand, the Republic of Korea, along with Taiwan as a key partner of Palau, will support the development and operation of a new, modern hospital facility, subject to the outcomes of the project feasibility study, ensuring it meets the long-term health and infrastructure needs of the Palauan people.  This partnership demonstrates our enduring commitment to Pacific partners and to the shared development principles that underpin a resilient and prosperous region.
  • Upgrading Penrhyn (Omoka) Port: The U.S. Department of State, working with Congress and in partnership with New Zealand and the Cook Islands, intends to upgrade the Penrhyn atoll’s Omoka Port.  This project builds on the Critical Minerals Framework the United States and the Cook Islands signed in February 2026 and will deliver safety and security benefits and expand transport links and economic opportunities for the Cook Islands and American people.
  • Strengthening Transportation Linkages in the Marshall Islands: USTDA has approved funding for technical assistance for the Marshall Islands Ports Authority to help modernize the country’s two primary ports: Majuro and Ebeye. The project’s goals are to increase freight capacity, improve port efficiency, and strengthen supply chain reliability. USTDA has also approved funding for technical assistance to help modernize the Amata Kabua International Airport, including airfield and terminal facilities. The assistance will address anticipated growth and operational improvements over a 20-year horizon and facilitate aviation partnership opportunities for U.S. industry.

Expanding Commercial Diplomacy

  • Second Pacific Investment Summit: The inaugural U.S.-Pacific Islands Investment Summit at the East-West Center in Honolulu in February 2026 generated several successful economic opportunities and business deals for U.S. and Pacific Islands businesses across several sectors including infrastructure, critical minerals, supply chains, energy, tourism, food security, financial services, and the digital economy.  To continue to foster U.S.-Pacific Islands private sector connections and investments, the United States intends to support a second summit to be held in early 2027.

Promoting Trusted Digital Technology

  • Data Center Infrastructure for Tonga: USTDA, with funding from the U.S. Department of State, is supporting a feasibility study to modernize Tonga’s national data center and network, enabling secure, resilient hosting for government systems and public services. The study advances a broader U.S. effort to build Tonga’s digital infrastructure on trusted American technology, alongside State Department support for secure cloud migration.
  • Mobile Network Modernization for the Marshall Islands: USTDA, with funding from the U.S. Department of State, will provide technical assistance to support the modernization of the nationwide mobile network in the Republic of the Marshall Islands. The assistance will identify optimal technology options, financing pathways and implementation strategies for the Marshall Islands National Telecommunications Authority.
  • Cloud Global Pacific Program: The U.S. Department of State plans to expand upon successful programming in Tonga and Palau to accelerate additional Pacific Island governments’ adoption of resilient cloud-based technologies. Adopting trusted cloud services expands the digital economy, creates opportunities for economic prosperity, strengthens cybersecurity, and increases operational continuity.
  • Secure Telecom Regulation and Digital Transformation Programs in the Pacific Islands: S. Department’s Bureau of Cyberspace and Digital Policy (CDP) has funded a series of programs, coordinated by the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Commercial Law Development Program (CLDP), to strengthen ICT regulatory capacity, expand digital infrastructure, and modernize regulatory and licensing models, including a PNG Secure ICT Investment Screening Workshop and Pacific Islands Telecom Regulator Workshop, and Study Tour.  Additionally, CDP led the U.S.-Pacific Islands Digital Transformation Accelerator conference, held alongside the Pacific Islands Telecom Regulators’ Forum, generating 32 matchmaking sessions between U.S. technology companies and PIC governments, advancing potential leads for U.S. AI exports and digital sector investment.  

Advancing Law Enforcement Cooperation and Maritime Security

  • U.S.-Pacific Islands Conference of Police Ministers (COPMIN): The United States and Palau will co-chair the inaugural U.S.-Pacific Islands Conference of Police Ministers (COPMIN).  COPMIN will focus on maritime security, drug trafficking, and cybercrime, and illicit finance.
  • Pacific Regional IUU Fishing Project: The U.S. Department of State, working with Congress, plans to provide $17 million to counter illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing in the Pacific Islands, focused on legal support to update national laws, policies, and regulations to align to regional IUU fishing strategic objectives, develop compliance officer capacity through certified training programs, and deploy new technologies to increase non-human monitoring capacity.

Deepening Scientific and Technical Cooperation

  • Seabed Mapping, Exploration, and Characterization: The U.S. Department of State, working with Congress, plans to provide support for seabed mapping, exploration, and characterization to inform Pacific Island government decision making on potential seabed minerals development within national jurisdiction and related national regulatory frameworks.
  • Drinking Water Sampling Project: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), in partnership with Taiwan, will work with Palau to conduct a comprehensive drinking water sampling project on the island’s drinking water sources and wells. The project will also provide training for Palau drinking water operators and environmental lab regulatory staff on proper sampling and logistical techniques.  

Expanding People to People Ties

  • Peace Corps Letter of Intent to Return to Compact of Free Association Nations: The Peace Corps has signed a letter of intent to establish the North Pacific program with the Federated States of Micronesia, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the Republic of Palau.  This step builds on decades of partnership: more than 4,400 Volunteers served in Micronesia and Palau between 1966 and 2018, and more than 140 served in the Marshall Islands from 1966 to 1996.  The agency completed its re-opening of Peace Corps/Palau in July 2026.

item.title: Vietnam National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Vietnam National Day

Press Statement

September 1, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I extend my warmest congratulations to the Government and people of Vietnam as you celebrate your 81st National Day on September 2.

This day honors Vietnam’s independence – an enduring testament to the strength and resilience of its people. The United States values its flourishing partnership with Vietnam, particularly the progress achieved under our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and our shared commitment to peace and stability across the Indo-Pacific region.

We commend Vietnam’s growing leadership as a partner to the United States, including its distinguished role as a founding member supporting the Board of Peace. As we reflect on Vietnam’s remarkable achievements, we look forward to building on this progress and working together to ensure shared prosperity and security for our peoples in the years ahead.

On this special occasion, I send my congratulations to Vietnam and my best wishes for a year of continued success, peace, and prosperity.

item.title: Trump Administration Launches Foundry School to Build the Workforce Behind America’s Manufacturing Comeback
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Trump Administration Launches Foundry School to Build the Workforce Behind America’s Manufacturing Comeback

Notice to the Press

September 1, 2026

On Thursday, September 3, the Trump Administration will launch Foundry School, a national program to train the entrepreneurs, engineers, technicians, and industrial leaders needed to rebuild American manufacturing. Vice President JD Vance will headline the launch event. Foundry School is a project of Pax Silica, the Department’s flagship multilateral initiative to secure trusted global supply chains for the technologies that will define the next century.

President Trump’s reindustrialization agenda has already brought trillions of dollars in industrial investment to American soil. Foundry School will focus on turning that investment into jobs. American manufacturers will need an estimated 3.8 million skilled workers by 2033 in semiconductors, defense, energy, and beyond, and Foundry School exists to make sure Americans fill those jobs. The program will put American workers first by equipping them with the skills needed to bring manufacturing jobs home and build careers in industries critical to our nation’s economic security.

The launch event, which begins at 8:20 a.m. at the Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace, will feature remarks by senior Administration officials, university leaders and industry executives, as well as a photo opportunity.

Foundry School was announced as a Pax Silica initiative by Under Secretary Helberg at the Pax Summit on June 25, 2026. Announced as a workforce development partnership with Stanford University, Foundry School is anchored in a first-of-its-kind advanced manufacturing curriculum for American students developed by Stanford that also features keystone lectures provided by seven universities with which Stanford has collaborated. Those universities are Arizona State University, Georgia Tech, Ohio State University, Penn State, the University of Cincinnati, the University of Kansas, and Vanderbilt University. Across these eight campuses, the program will run 17 sessions, each taught by founders and CEOs from advanced manufacturing enterprises. These leaders will be drawn from the United States and Pax Silica participants, including the Republic of Korea, Japan, Taiwan, and India, covering everything it takes to build and run a world-class manufacturing enterprise. It is a single course to ensure that the American workforce benefits from America’s industrial renaissance.

Interested media must apply for credentials at the following link by 9:00 a.m. on Wednesday, September 2. Space is limited. Submissions for credentials do not guarantee access to the event. Further details, including location and access instructions, will be sent to registered media prior to the day of the event.

For media inquiries, please submit a request.

item.title: United States Welcomes Türkiye’s Signing of the Artemis Accords
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

United States Welcomes Türkiye’s Signing of the Artemis Accords

Media Note

September 1, 2026

The Department of State congratulates the Republic of Türkiye on joining the Artemis Accords. Türkiye is the 71st country to sign the Accords to date, pledging its commitment to peaceful exploration and use of space.

Türkiye’s Minister of Industry and Technology Mehmet Fatih Kacır signed the Accords on behalf of the Republic of Türkiye on August 31, 2026. U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for Space and Environment Connor Tomlinson and NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman witnessed and celebrated the signing at a ceremony at the Mary W. Jackson NASA Headquarters in Washington, D.C. Türkiye is a long standing and valued NATO ally with which the United States closely coordinates on defense cooperation, regional security, and commercial partnerships.

The United States and seven other countries established the Artemis Accords in 2020 in President Trump’s first term, to serve as a set of practical principles to guide responsible space exploration. Türkiye joins the United States and 69 other nations in affirming the Accords’ principles for sustainable civil space activity. The Department of State and NASA lead the United States’ outreach and implementation of the Accords.

For more information, including a full list of signatories to the Accords, please visit the Artemis Accords webpage. Interested members of the media can submit a press inquiry.

item.title: Slovakia National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Slovakia National Day

Press Statement

September 1, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I congratulate the people of Slovakia as you mark Constitution Day.

The United States and Slovakia share a strong partnership built on mutual respect, shared responsibility, and the principle that sovereign nations are strongest when they are free to make their own choices and defend their own interests.

Over the past year, we have deepened this partnership through our cooperation on Slovakia’s military modernization efforts and in the field of civil nuclear energy. These efforts make both our nations stronger and contribute to a more secure and prosperous transatlantic community.

My visit to Bratislava earlier this year reaffirmed the importance the United States places in our relationship with Slovakia. We look forward to building on that momentum by expanding trade and investment, advancing our shared energy and security interests, and pursuing practical cooperation that benefits both the American and Slovak people.

item.title: Joint Statement on Penrhyn Port Project
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Joint Statement on Penrhyn Port Project

Media Note

August 31, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America, Cook Islands, and New Zealand on the announcement of the Penrhyn Port Project.

Begin Text

The United States, the Cook Islands, and New Zealand intend to partner to deliver a major port upgrade on the island of Penrhyn in the northern Cook Islands, senior representatives announced today.

Cook Islands Prime Minister Mark Brown, New Zealand Foreign Minister Winston Peters, and U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau announced the project in Palau ahead of the Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting.

The United States and New Zealand intend to co-fund the project. The U.S. Department of State, working with Congress, will contribute US$50 million (approximately $NZ84 million) and New Zealand will contribute $NZ17.5 million (approximately US$10 million). New Zealand will implement the project in close coordination with the Cook Islands and the United States.

“This is a positive and hugely significant initiative that demonstrates the strength of New Zealand’s partnerships with both the Cook Islands and the United States,” Mr. Peters says.

“We are very pleased to be able to partner with the United States and the Cook Islands Governments to deliver this development priority for the Cook Islands, drawing on New Zealand’s experience in infrastructure delivery across the Pacific.”

“This project underscores the United States’ strong commitment to our partners in the Pacific and builds on the Critical Minerals Framework the United States and the Cook Islands signed earlier this year,” Deputy Secretary Landau says.

“It also highlights our historic ties to Penrhyn atoll, where U.S. personnel constructed Penrhyn’s port and airstrip over 80 years ago.  Through transformational infrastructure initiatives such as this, we are making the United States and our partners safer, stronger, and more prosperous.”

“This port is a lifeline for Tongareva allowing for safer landings, better access to services, and stronger connections between our Pa Enua and the world. This wharf upgrade complements our new domestic shipping investments and our own efforts in improving transport connections for our Pa Enua. We thank the United States and New Zealand for partnering with us to deliver on a priority our people have themselves identified,” Prime Minister Brown says.

Penrhyn (also called Tongareva) is the northernmost island in the Cook Islands, and its port is at the village of Omoka. Upgraded port facilities will deliver safety and security benefits, as well as expand transport links and economic opportunities for the northern Cook Islands.

End Text

item.title: Uzbekistan Independence Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Uzbekistan Independence Day

Press Statement

August 31, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I extend warm congratulations to the people of Uzbekistan as they celebrate 35 years of independence on September 1.

The U.S.-Uzbekistan strategic partnership is producing meaningful results across a range of shared priorities. From critical minerals, energy, and infrastructure, to aviation, finance, and technology, American and Uzbek businesses are expanding commercial ties and creating new opportunities for our two countries. The United States welcomes Uzbekistan’s tenure as the C5+1 Secretariat co-chair (2026-2027) and collaborative efforts to further strengthen regional security, connectivity, and economic growth.

As Uzbekistan celebrates this important milestone, the United States looks forward to building on this momentum and deepening a partnership that makes both our countries stronger, more secure, and more prosperous.

The United States welcomes Uzbekistan’s tenure as the C5+1 Secretariat co-chair (2026-2027) and collaborative efforts to further strengthen regional security, connectivity, and economic growth.

As Uzbekistan celebrates this important milestone, the United States looks forward to building on this momentum and deepening a partnership that makes both our countries stronger, more secure, and more prosperous.

On behalf of the United States, I congratulate the people of Trinidad and Tobago as they celebrate 64 years of independence.

The United States and Trinidad and Tobago share a longstanding partnership built on a mutual commitment to regional prosperity. Today, our relationship is stronger than ever as we work together to combat transnational crime, strengthen regional security, as well as support energy resilience and cooperation that benefits both our countries.

As you commemorate this important milestone, we celebrate the enduring friendship between our nations and look forward to continuing to advance our shared priorities and build an even stronger partnership in the years ahead.

item.title: Iceland’s August 29 Referendum
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesperson

Iceland’s August 29 Referendum

Press Statement

August 30, 2026

The United States takes note of Iceland’s August 29 Referendum on whether to resume EU accession negotiations. We respect the sovereign decision of the people of Iceland and express confidence in Iceland’s continuing trajectory as a strong and valuable NATO ally and close partner of the United States and Europe. We look forward to strengthening our partnership with Iceland on all fronts including security, energy, innovation, and economic and cultural ties, to further advance our shared vision of peace and prosperity.
